title: Tutorial Tours run as a modal on whatever screen you are on and tell you to click tabs that are not there -- and the modal blocks every one of them
reasoning: Reproduced live on display :83, profile v2-settings-system. Settings > Help & Tutorials > Tutorial Tours > Equipment Setup > Start renders a centred modal with a full-screen scrim ON the Settings screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-05.png). Step 1 reads 'Equipment Profiles / Click the Profiles tab to manage your equipment configurations.' -- there is no Profiles tab on Settings. With the overlay up I clicked the left-nav 'Imaging' entry; the tree afterwards still reported 'Tutorial step 1 of 4: Equipment Profiles [DISABLED]' with Settings > Help & Tutorials underneath, i.e. the scrim swallowed the click and no navigation happened. Code matches the cited location: help_tutorials_settings.dart:179-180 onStart -> notifier.restartTutorial(TutorialCategory.equipmentSetup); tutorial_provider.dart:640 _restartTutorial only writes activeCategory/currentStepIndex and never routes. Secondary observation: the row still reads 'Not started' while the tour is running.

title: The desktop app can never tell you a new version exists: the only 'Updates' page in Settings is for a remote appliance, and the built-in update manager is wired to a server URL nothing ever sets
reasoning: Live: Settings search 'update' returns exactly two entries, About and Appliance Updates. Appliance Updates renders only a title, 'Check for, stage, and apply updates to the connected rig' and one info panel 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its updates. The local desktop app updates itself through its own installer.' -- no controls. About renders Skotiq / Version 6.1.0 / tagline / GitHub / Documentation / Report an Issue / System Information (Platform, OS Version, Dart Version) -- no update control, no build number. Code confirms the dead path at the cited locations: app.dart:204-206 wraps the desktop shell in UpdateManagerWidget; update_manager_widget.dart:39-43 _isUpdateConfigured() and :163-168 _checkForUpdates return early when updateProvider.state.updateServerUrl is null/empty; the only call to UpdateNotifier.configure/UpdateService.configure outside the updater package's own controller is apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/update_wiring.dart:79, reached from desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:377 which builds a SEPARATE UpdateService for the headless API server and requires SKOTIQ_UPDATE_SERVER to be set -- it never touches the Riverpod updateProvider the GUI widget reads. So the GUI check is inert on a shipped build.

title: Remote Access claims 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine' -- localhost is not exempt from auth at all
reasoning: Reproduced live. Enabled remote access on port 8391 (bound 0.0.0.0:8391, verified with ss). From 127.0.0.1: GET /api/status -> 401 {"error":"Authentication required","message":"Missing Authorization header or session cookie"}; /api/images/recent -> 401; /api/auth/csrf -> 401; /api/system/info -> 401. Only GET /dashboard is 200 (static shell). The three copy strings are still live on the page: the footer note (tree + /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-15.png), the 'Open on this computer / Use this link from the same machine to confirm the dashboard is working before sharing it elsewhere' card, and Connection details -> Authentication: 'Paired devices required remotely'. Locations check out: translations.dart:389 is remoteAccessInfoBody ('Localhost stays frictionless...') and :398-399 is remoteAccessLocalActionTitle/Body. Enforcement: http_middleware.dart's auth chain has no peer-address branch -- the only 'loopback' mentions in that file are about the rate-limit trusted-proxy header and CORS, and the token==null -> 401 return at :759-771 fires regardless of peer.

title: After a device pairs successfully the desktop keeps showing the pairing code counting down, and the device list does not update
reasoning: Reproduced live. Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > Start Pairing Mode; code NEBULA-MOON-4612 read from pairing_sessions. POST /api/pairing/verify -> 200 with a bearer token; a second verify with the same code -> 401 invalid_pairing_code, so the server destroyed it immediately. paired_devices went 13 -> 14 active rows. The desktop screen did not react: 5s later and again ~60s later the tree still read 'Enter this code on your device: / Expires in 04:35 / ... 04:18 / Cancel Pairing', and the list still rendered 13 'Paired:' rows against the DB's 14. Location is right: pairing_screen.dart:94-96 _initialize() is the constructor-time load, :215 loadPairedDevices, and the only other caller is the manual refresh IconButton at :484 -- nothing subscribes to pairing completion.

title: Paired devices always say 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' -- last_connected_at is never written
reasoning: Reproduced live. After pairing device_id v2-probe-adv I made three authenticated GET /api/status calls with its bearer (200, 200, 200) and held an authenticated WebSocket on /events (HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols; ESTAB in ss for minutes). sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/v2-settings-system/data/pairing.db 'select device_id,last_connected_at from paired_devices' -> last_connected_at is NULL for v2-probe-adv and for all 13 other rows, and every UI row reads 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet'. Root cause is a little more precise than the finding states: the write DOES exist (pairing_database.dart:138 updateLastConnected) and its only non-test caller is token_manager.dart:297 inside TokenManager.verifySessionToken -- which the HTTP auth path never calls. The desktop server authenticates from its own in-memory BoundedTokenGrantMap _pairedSessionTokens (declared headless_api_server.dart:233, hydrated from Drift at server_lifecycle.dart:366, compared in http_middleware.dart:1030), so no request ever reaches the code that stamps the timestamp.

title: 'Active Viewers' on the Remote Access page counts co-imaging collaborators, not connected remote clients -- it stays 0 with a live dashboard socket open
reasoning: Reproduced live. With a paired client holding an authenticated WebSocket on /events (101 Switching Protocols; ss shows the ESTAB pair on :8391 for the whole window) Connection details read 'Active Viewers 0' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-15.png). Code confirms it cannot be anything else: web_server_provider.dart:193 setActiveViewers is the only mutator of WebServerState.activeViewers, and its only call site in the entire non-test tree is desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:348, inside a listener on nextServer.collaborationManager.stream that assigns collabState.viewers.length -- CollaborationViewer is the live co-imaging session participant type (live_collaboration_session.dart:69). The same field drives the status-bar chip (screens/shell/widgets/status_bar/session_sharing.dart:19,70,177-203). All three cited locations are accurate.

title: Settings search sends 'license' and 'credits' to About, which contains neither
reasoning: Static: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_catalog.dart:205-214 still declares the About section with keywords ['version','license','credits','updates','build']. about_settings.dart (read in full) renders only: logo, 'Skotiq', 'Version <appVersion.version>', tagline, three link buttons and a System Information card with Platform / OS Version / Dart Version. No licence text, no third-party credits, no showLicensePage/LicenseRegistry anywhere under screens/settings, and no build number (AppVersionInfo.buildNumber exists but About prints only .version). Location as cited is accurate.

title: GLADE+ catalog download is broken end to end: the VizieR TAP endpoint it targets returns 503, and the app's only report of that is a snackbar you cannot see
reasoning: The download works. I reproduced the exact query buildGladePlusUrl() emits for the Standard tier (source_models.dart:340-356, still targeting https://tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr/TAPVizieR/tap/sync) with curl: HTTP 200, 4,874,018 bytes of CSV in 9.2 s. Then I drove the UI: Settings > Catalogs > GLADE+ > 'Download Standard (~50 MB)' -- the button went to 'Downloading...' with a 'Downloading: GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog' progress panel, glade_plus_galaxies.csv.partial grew, and the run finished with glade_plus_galaxies.csv at 15,635,359 bytes. No error, no failure snackbar. The 503 the finding measured was a transient VizieR outage, not an app defect, so 'cannot be fetched at all, on any tier' does not hold. Two residuals worth noting separately (neither is this finding): the tier is labelled '~50 MB' but delivers ~15.6 MB, and the download bypasses SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely -- it wrote into the developer's real ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/catalogs/ from a sandboxed instance. The single-mirror fragility the finding raises is a design concern, not a reproducible defect.

This is separate from the phone's own planetarium catalogs.' The live tree shows no button, no picker and no link anywhere on the page. Source confirms: rig_catalog_settings.dart:281-289, the `if (backend == null)` branch renders a bare _Info with that text and no action; the desktop build hard-codes 'the phone's'.
location_wrong: The finding gave no file. Precise location: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/rig_catalog_settings.dart:276-289.

title: The in-app Logs viewer records nothing about the failures the user just watched happen -- five failed catalog downloads and every rejected save are absent from it and from the 18.8 MB log export
reasoning: Confirmed on this session's own failures, with one correction to the specifics. In this run I produced three user-visible 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: ...' snackbars, two rejected profile saves ('Focal length must be a positive number'), one unhandled 'Cannot activate profile 6' exception, and one successful 15.6 MB GLADE+ download. Settings > Logs then reported: search 'duplicat' -> 0 of 124 entries; 'download' -> 0 of 124; 'glade' -> 0 of 124; 'catalog' -> 1; 'profile' -> 2. The single error-level line for the whole session is '[ProfileActivationWriteThrough] Strict activation aborted: target profile 6 does not exist' -- exactly the shape the finding described. I then pressed Export and grepped the 19,489,798-byte / 147,939-line result: 0 occurrences of 'glade', 0 of 'duplicat', 0 of 'annotation catalog'. Mechanism matches the cited location: catalog_settings_screen.dart:1229-1230 catches and calls _showError, which is only context.showErrorSnackBar (:414-418) with no logger call; the duplicate handler does the same at screen_shell.dart:394. Correction to the finding's framing: the catalog download SUCCEEDED this time and still produced no log entry at all, so the gap is 'no catalog-download logging, success or failure', not only the failure path.

reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Settings > Logs > Export, from an instance launched with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/v2-settings-system/data, wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/skotiq_logs_2026-08-03T17-11-30.txt -- 19,489,798 bytes, 147,939 lines. No file picker, no size estimate, no confirmation; the only notice is the log line 'Logs exported to: <path>'. The file concatenates every rotated on-disk log back to 2026-07-28 (section headers '=== /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs/skotiq.log.2026-07-28 ===' through 2026-08-03, then '=== In-memory Dart log entries ==='), so it also reads from the real user log dir rather than the sandbox. ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports/ contains only unrelated CSV/HTML session exports. Location is right: log_viewer.dart:241-276 _exportLogs builds the path as '${docsDir.path}/skotiq_logs_$timestamp.txt' at :262 with no picker.

title: Deleting your last equipment profile leaves a ghost profile on screen whose 'Set Active' throws an unhandled exception and does nothing
reasoning: Reproduced live end to end. With exactly one profile left ('Adv Rig One (Copy)'), overflow > Delete > Delete drove equipment_profiles to 0 rows (sqlite3 confirmed) and the middle column correctly showed 'No profiles yet' -- while the right pane kept rendering the deleted profile in full: name, f/5.0, 530 mm, 106 mm, both filters, focus offsets, plus a live 'Set Active' button and a live overflow menu (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-36.png). Clicking Set Active produced no toast and no visible change; the log shows exactly the claimed unhandled exception with a stack trace that matches all three cited locations verbatim: 'Unhandled Exception: Bad state: Cannot activate profile 6: no such profile row (strict activation requires an existing target)' at profile_activation_writethrough.dart:156 <- profiles_provider.dart:980 _activateProfile <- screen_shell.dart:232. Not separately re-tested this pass: the Edit-then-Save 'Profile not found' half of the report.

title: Filter Focus Offsets silently omits the filter you just added -- you cannot set an offset for it without saving and re-opening the editor
reasoning: Reproduced live on a fresh profile 'Adv Rig One'. In Edit, typing 'Lum' into the (single, pre-seeded) filter chip produced NO Filter Focus Offsets section at all -- the section only appeared after I pressed '+', which forced a rebuild. Then, with chips 'Lum | Ha', typing 'Ha' into the second chip left Filter Focus Offsets listing only 'Lum' with no input for Ha (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-24.png, and full-page /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-27.png). Save + re-open Edit made both Lum and Ha rows appear (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-28.png). Mechanism as described: profile_details_helpers.dart:155-166 builds the offset rows by reading _filterControllers[i].text, and the filter-name TextField has no onChanged, so nothing calls setState when the name is typed.
location_wrong: First half is right (profile_details_helpers.dart:154-165 is the offsets loop). Second half is off: the filter-name TextField that lacks onChanged is _EditableFilterChip in profile_controls.dart:306-321, not profile_details_rendering.dart:449-500 -- that range is only where the chip is instantiated (:486-492).

title: Duplicate reports 'Duplicate profile failed' for a duplicate that succeeded, and leaks an internal invariant message to the user
reasoning: Reproduced live, 3 times out of 5 duplicates of the same source profile. Duplicates 1 and 2 succeeded silently; duplicates 3, 4 and 5 each showed the snackbar 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 4 / 5 / 6 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' while sqlite3 showed equipment_profiles rows 4, 5 and 6 present and the profile list in the same screen rendered all of them (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-31.png shows five 'Adv Rig One (Copy)' rows). Both halves of the message are false exactly as claimed. It is a post-write refresh race: screen_shell.dart:311-324 _awaitMutatedProfile awaits ref.read(equipmentProfilesProvider.future) after duplicateProfile's ref.invalidateSelf() and throws a StateError when the id is not yet in the returned list; the assertion text (naming a row id and an internal list) goes straight to showErrorSnackBar at :394.
location_wrong: Cited 'the duplicate handler in .../profile_controls.dart'; the duplicate handler and the message are both in .../equipment_profiles_screen_parts/screen_shell.dart -- _duplicateProfile at :362-396, _awaitMutatedProfile (the throw) at :311-324, the snackbar at :394. profile_controls.dart holds unrelated widgets (_EditableFilterChip, _DeviceChip).

title: Duplicate happily creates two profiles with byte-identical names, while Import de-duplicates -- so the profile list can show rows nothing can tell apart
reasoning: Reproduced live. Duplicating 'Adv Rig One' five times, accepting the pre-filled name every time, produced ids 2,3,4,5,6 all named exactly 'Adv Rig One (Copy)' (sqlite3 output) and the list renders five visually identical rows with the same icon and no subtitle (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-31.png). The offered name is a fixed '${profile.name} (Copy)' built at screen_shell.dart:368 with no collision check, whereas the profile importer resolves collisions with a '(n)' suffix. Severity is fair at P3 -- it is a usability/consistency defect, not data loss.

title: The 'default startup profile' that Settings > General promises has no UI anywhere -- it is pinned to whichever profile you created first
reasoning: All three parts reproduced live. (1) Settings > General still reads 'Auto-connect equipment / Connects the default startup profile on launch, falling back to the last active profile when no default is set' (read from the live tree). (2) Equipment Profiles exposes no default affordance: the badge is 'Active', the header action is 'Set Active', and the overflow menu is exactly Edit / Duplicate / Export / Delete (read from the live Popup menu tree and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-21.png). (3) The flag does not follow activation: after creating profile 1 (is_active=1, is_default=1), duplicating it five times (all is_default=0) and pressing Set Active on profile 2, sqlite3 shows 1|Adv Rig One|is_active=0|is_default=1 and 2|Adv Rig One (Copy)|is_active=1|is_default=0. So the rig the copy says will be connected on launch is not the one the operator just activated, and no screen can see or change it.

title: Backup & Restore contradicts itself about what restore does -- one card says nothing is merged, the confirm dialog says nothing is deleted
reasoning: Both sentences are true of their own operation; the finding compared copy from two different restore paths. The 'Sync is bundle-based ... nothing is merged' paragraph belongs to CloudSyncCard (cloud_sync_settings.dart:377-378) and describes the WebDAV/S3 pull-and-restore, which really does replace: cloud_sync_settings.dart:324 calls service.pullAndRestore(..., replaceExisting: true) and its own confirm dialog (:313-314) repeats the replace wording. The 'without deleting your current data' dialog is ConfirmDialog.restore (utils/confirm_dialog.dart:88-100), used by backup_screen.dart:236 for a LOCAL Recent-Backups restore, which calls backupService.restoreBackup(replaceExisting: false) at backup_screen.dart:265-268 -- merge semantics, exactly as the dialog says. The verifier's own experiment (canary survives, profile returns) is the documented behaviour of the local path, so it does not show the sync sentence is false. The cited 'where' is also wrong: backup_screen.dart contains neither string.
location_wrong: Cited packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart; the two strings actually live in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/cloud_sync_settings.dart:313-314,377-378 and packages/skotiq_app/lib/utils/confirm_dialog.dart:96-98.
